column1: Marie Curie is probably the most famous woman scientist who has ever lived.
column2: 玛丽·居里可能是有史以来最著名的女科学家。
column6: who has ever lived|有史以来的

column1: Born Maria Sklodowska in Poland in 1867, she is famous for her work on radioactivity, and was twice a winner of the Nobel Prize.
column2: 她于1867年出生在波兰，原名玛丽亚·斯克沃多夫斯卡。她因研究放射性而闻名，曾两次获得诺贝尔奖。

column1: With her husband, Pierre Curie, and Henri Becquerel, she was awarded the 1903 Nobel Prize for Physics, and was then sole winner of the 1911 Nobel Prize for Chemistry.
column2: 她与丈夫皮埃尔·居里、亨利·贝克勒尔共同获得了1903年的诺贝尔物理学奖，随后又独自获得了1911年的诺贝尔化学奖。
column4: Nobel Prize for Physics|诺贝尔物理学奖
column6: Nobel Prize for Chemistry|诺贝尔化学奖

column1: She was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize.
column2: 她是第一位获得诺贝尔奖的女性。
column3: first woman to|第一位做……的女性

column1: From childhood, Marie was remarkable for her prodigious memory, and at the age of 16 won a gold medal on completion of her secondary education.
column2: 玛丽从小就以惊人的记忆力引人注目。16岁完成中学学业时，她获得了一枚金牌。

column1: Because her father lost his savings through bad investment, she then had to take work as a teacher.
column2: 父亲因投资失利损失了积蓄，于是她不得不当老师。

column1: From her earnings she was able to finance her sister Bronia’s medical studies in Paris, on the understanding that Bronia would, in turn, later help her to get an education.
column2: 她靠自己的收入资助姐姐布罗尼娅在巴黎学医，两人约定，日后布罗尼娅也会反过来帮助她接受教育。
column6: on the understanding that|双方约定

column1: In 1891 this promise was fulfilled and Marie went to Paris and began to study at the Sorbonne (the University of Paris).
column2: 1891年，这一承诺兑现了。玛丽前往巴黎，开始在索邦大学（巴黎大学）学习。
column7: the University of Paris|巴黎大学

column1: She often worked far into the night and lived on little more than bread and butter and tea.
column2: 她经常工作到深夜，平日几乎只靠面包、黄油和茶过活。
column4: far into the night|直到深夜

column1: She came first in the examination in the physical sciences in 1893, and in 1894 was placed second in the examination in mathematical sciences.
column2: 1893年，她在物理科学考试中获得第一名，1894年又在数学考试中获得第二名。

column1: It was not until the spring of that year that she was introduced to Pierre Curie.
column2: 直到那年春天，她才经人介绍认识了皮埃尔·居里。

column1: Their marriage in 1895 marked the start of a partnership that was soon to achieve results of world significance.
column2: 两人于1895年结婚，由此开始了合作，并很快取得了具有世界意义的成果。
column4: marked the start of|标志着……的开始

column1: Following Henri Becquerel’s discovery in 1896 of a new phenomenon, which Marie later called ‘radioactivity’, Marie Curie decided to find out if the radioactivity discovered in uranium was to be found in other elements.
column2: 1896年亨利·贝克勒尔发现了一种新现象，玛丽后来将其称为“放射性”。在此之后，玛丽·居里决定弄清楚，铀中发现的放射性是否也存在于其他元素中。

column1: She discovered that this was true for thorium.
column2: 她发现，钍也具有放射性。
column4: this was true for|这一点也适用于

column1: Turning her attention to minerals, she found her interest drawn to pitchblende, a mineral whose radioactivity, superior to that of pure uranium, could be explained only by the presence in the ore of small quantities of an unknown substance of very high activity.
column2: 她转而关注矿物，对沥青铀矿产生了兴趣。这种矿物的放射性强于纯铀，唯一的解释是矿石中含有少量放射性极强的未知物质。
column3: Turning her attention to|转而关注
column14: very high activity|极强的放射性

column1: Pierre Curie joined her in the work that she had undertaken to resolve this problem, and that led to the discovery of the new elements, polonium and radium.
column2: 皮埃尔·居里加入了玛丽为解决这一问题而开展的研究，两人由此发现了钋和镭这两种新元素。
column3: joined her in|加入她，一同从事

column1: While Pierre Curie devoted himself chiefly to the physical study of the new radiations, Marie Curie struggled to obtain pure radium in the metallic state.
column2: 皮埃尔·居里主要致力于从物理学角度研究这些新发现的辐射，而玛丽·居里则费力地尝试获得金属态的纯镭。
column3: devoted himself chiefly to|主要致力于

column1: This was achieved with the help of the chemist Andre-Louis Debierne, one of Pierre Curie’s pupils.
column2: 她在化学家安德烈-路易·德比埃尔纳的帮助下做到了这一点。他是皮埃尔·居里的学生之一。
column4: with the help of|在……的帮助下

column1: Based on the results of this research, Marie Curie received her Doctorate of Science, and in 1903 Marie and Pierre shared with Becquerel the Nobel Prize for Physics for the discovery of radioactivity.
column2: 凭借这项研究成果，玛丽·居里获得了理学博士学位。1903年，玛丽和皮埃尔因发现放射性，与贝克勒尔共同获得诺贝尔物理学奖。
column6: Doctorate of Science|n. 理学博士学位
column8: Nobel Prize for Physics|n. 诺贝尔物理学奖

column1: The births of Marie’s two daughters, Irene and Eve, in 1897 and 1904 failed to interrupt her scientific work.
column2: 玛丽的两个女儿伊雷娜和艾芙分别于1897年和1904年出生。生育并没有中断她的科研工作。

column1: She was appointed lecturer in physics at the Ecole Normale Superieure for girls in Sevres, France (1900), and introduced a method of teaching based on experimental demonstrations.
column2: 1900年，她受聘在法国塞夫尔女子高等师范学校担任物理讲师，并引入了一种以实验演示为基础的教学方法。

column1: In December 1904 she was appointed chief assistant in the laboratory directed by Pierre Curie.
column2: 1904年12月，她被任命为皮埃尔·居里所主持的实验室的首席助理。

column1: The sudden death of her husband in 1906 was a bitter blow to Marie Curie, but was also a turning point in her career: henceforth she was to devote all her energy to completing alone the scientific work that they had undertaken.
column2: 丈夫在1906年猝然离世，给玛丽·居里以沉重打击，也成了她职业生涯的转折点。从此，她将全部精力投入两人先前共同开展的科学工作，独自将其完成。
column8: devote all her energy to|将全部精力投入

column1: On May 13, 1906, she was appointed to the professorship that had been left vacant on her husband’s death, becoming the first woman to teach at the Sorbonne.
column2: 1906年5月13日，她受命接任丈夫去世后空缺的教授职位，成为第一位在索邦大学任教的女性。
column6: on her husband’s death|在丈夫去世后

column1: In 1911 she was awarded the Nobel Prize for Chemistry for the isolation of a pure form of radium.
column2: 1911年，她因分离出纯镭而获得诺贝尔化学奖。
column4: Nobel Prize for Chemistry|n. 诺贝尔化学奖

column1: During World War I, Marie Curie, with the help of her daughter Irene, devoted herself to the development of the use of X-radiography, including the mobile units which came to be known as ‘Little Curies’, used for the treatment of wounded soldiers.
column2: 第一次世界大战期间，玛丽·居里在女儿伊雷娜的帮助下，致力于拓展X射线摄影的应用。其中包括后来被称为“小居里”的移动式设备，这些设备用于救治伤兵。
column3: World War I|第一次世界大战
column4: with the help of|在……的帮助下
column9: came to be known as|后来被称为

column1: In 1918 the Radium Institute, whose staff Irene had joined, began to operate in earnest, and became a centre for nuclear physics and chemistry.
column2: 伊雷娜已成为镭研究所的一员。1918年，研究所开始全面运作，后来成为核物理学和化学的研究中心。

column1: Marie Curie, now at the highest point of her fame and, from 1922, a member of the Academy of Medicine, researched the chemistry of radioactive substances and their medical applications.
column2: 此时，玛丽·居里的声望已达顶峰，她自1922年起又成为医学科学院院士。她研究了放射性物质的化学性质及其在医学上的应用。
column3: at the highest point of|处于……的顶峰
column6: Academy of Medicine|n. 医学科学院

column1: In 1921, accompanied by her two daughters, Marie Curie made a triumphant journey to the United States to raise funds for research on radium.
column2: 1921年，玛丽·居里在两个女儿的陪同下前往美国，为镭的研究筹款。这次访问大获成功。

column1: Women there presented her with a gram of radium for her campaign.
column2: 当地妇女赠给她一克镭，支持她的筹款活动。

column1: Marie also gave lectures in Belgium, Brazil, Spain and Czechoslovakia and, in addition, had the satisfaction of seeing the development of the Curie Foundation in Paris, and the inauguration in 1932 in Warsaw of the Radium Institute, where her sister Bronia became director.
column2: 玛丽还曾在比利时、巴西、西班牙和捷克斯洛伐克讲学。此外，令她欣慰的是，她看到巴黎居里基金会发展起来，也见证了华沙镭研究所于1932年正式成立。她的姐姐布罗尼娅在那里担任所长。

column1: One of Marie Curie’s outstanding achievements was to have understood the need to accumulate intense radioactive sources, not only to treat illness but also to maintain an abundant supply for research.
column2: 玛丽·居里的杰出成就之一，是认识到储备强放射源的必要性。这些放射源既可用于治疗疾病，也能为研究提供充足的供应。

column1: The existence in Paris at the Radium Institute of a stock of 1.5 grams of radium made a decisive contribution to the success of the experiments undertaken in the years around 1930.
column2: 巴黎镭研究所存有1.5克镭。这一储备对1930年前后所进行的实验取得成功起了决定性作用。
column10: in the years around|在……前后的几年里

column1: This work prepared the way for the discovery of the neutron by Sir James Chadwick and, above all, for the discovery in 1934 by Irene and Frederic Joliot-Curie of artificial radioactivity.
column2: 这项工作为詹姆斯·查德威克爵士发现中子铺平了道路，尤其为伊雷娜和弗雷德里克·约里奥-居里于1934年发现人工放射性铺平了道路。
column3: prepared the way for|为……铺平道路

column1: A few months after this discovery, Marie Curie died as a result of leukaemia caused by exposure to radiation.
column2: 这项发现之后数月，玛丽·居里因接触辐射所致的白血病去世。

column1: She had often carried test tubes containing radioactive isotopes in her pocket, remarking on the pretty blue-green light they gave off.
column2: 她常把装有放射性同位素的试管放在口袋里，还曾谈起它们发出的漂亮蓝绿色光芒。

column1: Her contribution to physics had been immense, not only in her own work, the importance of which had been demonstrated by her two Nobel Prizes, but because of her influence on subsequent generations of nuclear physicists and chemists.
column2: 她对物理学的贡献极大。这既体现在她自己的研究上，两次获诺贝尔奖足以说明这些研究的重要性，也体现在她对后世核物理学家和化学家的影响上。
